mutations.because: A frame is a fraction of the canvas in [0, 1] (D130), and the domain refuses anything else at both boundaries. Without the clamp a frame of 4 or -0.5 is written into the draft, the saved brief then fails validateTemplate, and the failure surfaces at packaging — far from the number input the user actually touched.

mutations.because: The string in a frame box and the number in the draft are not the same thing. Committing `Number(e.target.value)` on every keystroke turns an emptied field into `Number("") === 0` — a zero the user never typed, written to the frame the moment they cleared it to start again — and hands the reducer a NaN as soon as the box holds a half-typed value. Only a draft that parses to a finite number may leave the box.

mutations.after: // mutated: a run of copy typed into one element is no longer coalesced
mutations.because: Undo is measured in what the user did, not in keystrokes: without a coalescing key the element's copy costs one undo per character, so stepping back over a sentence takes as many presses as it has letters — and ⌘Z becomes a way to lose a word one letter at a time. The beat's copy has had the same key since VE1; an element's copy is the same edit.
